extracted.intended_audience: users of SINGULAR (decodegb.lib) — researchers and practitioners implementing algebraic decoding and coding-theory routines
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of procedures in the SINGULAR decodegb.lib library for coding/decoding tasks: each entry gives usage, parameter meanings, return values, assumptions, theoretical pointers, and examples illustrating how to construct ideals/systems for decoding problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: sysBin
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sysBin (v,Q,n,[odd]); v,n,odd are int, Q is list of int’s. - v a number if errors, - Q is a deﬁning set of the code, - n the length, - odd is an additional parameter: if set to 1, then the defining set is enlarged by odd elements, which are 2^(some power)*(some element in the def.set) mod n. Return: the ring with the resulting system called 'bin'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on Q of the given cyclic code, constructs corresponding ideal 'bin' using the Waring function to help solve the decoding problem. See theory pointer: Section C.8.3 [Generalized Newton identities]. Example provided for [31,16,7] quadratic residue code showing printed 'bin' equations. See also sysCRHT and sysNewton.

rubrics_metrics.name: encode
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: encode (x, g); x a row vector (message), and g a generator matrix. Return: corresponding codeword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows constructing a ring and generator matrix and calling encode to produce a codeword. Intended to encode a message vector using a given generator matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: syndrome
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: syndrome (h, c); h a check matrix, c a row vector (codeword). Return: corresponding syndrome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates constructing check matrix and codeword, disturbing the codeword and computing syndrome; shows expected syndrome vectors (all zeros for a valid codeword).

rubrics_metrics.name: sysQE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sysQE(check,y,t,[ﬁeldeq,formal]); check,y matrix; t,ﬁeldeq,formal int. - check is a parity check matrix of the code - y is a received word, - t the number of errors to be corrected, - if ﬁeldeq=1, field equations are added, - if formal=0, field equations on known syndrome variables are not added; to add them set formal>0 (exponent should equal number of elements in initial alphabet). Return: the ring to work with together with the resulting system called 'qe'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs an ideal from 'check' enabling computation of unknown syndromes of received word y; after unknown syndromes are obtained one can solve the decoding problem. Based on decoding method using quadratic equations (Section C.8.5). Example shows generation of 'qe' and subsequent Groebner basis reduction to solve for variables; option(redSB) and computing std(qe) shown. See also sysFL.

rubrics_metrics.name: errorInsert
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: errorInsert(y,pos,val); y is matrix, pos,val are list of int’s. - y is a (code) word, - pos = positions where errors occurred, - val = their corresponding values. Return: corresponding received word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows how to disturb an encoded word by inserting errors at specified positions and how to compute the difference (rec - y). Useful to simulate received words with known error positions/values for testing decoding routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: errorRand
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: errorRand(y, num, e); y is matrix, num,e are int. - y is a (code) word, - num is the number of errors, - e is an extension degree (if one wants values to be from GF(p^e)). Return: corresponding received word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows disturbing an encoded word with a given number of random errors (possibly over an extension field) to create test received words for decoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomCheck
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: randomCheck(m, n, e); m,n,e are int. - m x n are dimensions of the matrix, - e is an extension degree. Return: random check matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: generate a random check matrix for a [15,5] binary code (set e=1). Shows also computing corresponding generator matrix via dual_code. Useful for experiments with random codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: genMDSMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: genMDSMat(n, a); n is int, a is number. - n x n are dimensions of the MDS matrix, - a is a primitive element of the field. Return: a matrix with the MDS property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: constructs an MDS (Vandermonde) matrix using 'a' as a generator of the field's multiplicative group. Assumes extension field already defined. Example prints the Vandermonde matrix. See Section C.8.5 for theory relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: mindist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mindist (check, q); check matrix, q int. - check is a check matrix, - q is the field size. Return: minimum distance of the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing the minimum distance of a code given its check matrix and field size; result is used to derive error-correction capacity (e.g., (d-1)/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: decode
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: decode(check, rec, t); check, rec matrix, t int. - check is the check matrix of the code, - rec is a received word, - t is an upper bound for the number of errors one wants to correct. Note: method described in Section C.8.5 is used. Assume: errors in rec should be correctable, otherwise output is unpredictable. Return: a codeword that is closest to rec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows generating random check matrix, creating a codeword, disturbing it, then decoding and printing the decoded word. Emphasizes that decode relies on quadratic-equation-based method and requires errors to be within correctable bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: decodeRandom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: decodeRandom(redun,q,ncodes,ntrials,[e]); all parameters int. - redun is redundancy of a (random) code, - q is the field size, - ncodes is number of random codes to process, - ntrials is number of received vectors per code to be corrected, - If e is given it sets the correction capacity explicitly; otherwise procedure tries to compute the real minimum distance to find error-correction capacity. Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown: runs decoding experiments on many random codes/trials and prints check matrices, codewords, received words and Groebner bases of the QE system; useful for benchmarking decoding over ensembles of random codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: decodeCode
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: decodeCode(check, ntrials, [e]); check matrix, ntrials,e int. - check is a parity check matrix for the code, - ntrials is the number of received vectors per code to be corrected. - If e is given it sets the correction capacity explicitly; otherwise procedure tries to compute the real minimum distance. Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs multiple decoding trials for a given code (check matrix). Example shows printed Groebner bases and codeword/received pairs; intended for testing a specific code over many random perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: vanishId
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vanishId (points); points is a list of matrices (points). Return: Vanishing ideal corresponding to the given set of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows generating all 3-vectors over GF(3), selecting a subset of points, and constructing the vanishing ideal; prints generators like x(1)*x(2), x(1)^2-x(1), etc. Useful when constructing ideals of evaluation points for algebraic decoding or interpolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: sysFL
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sysFL (check,y,t,e,s); check,y matrix, t,e,s int. - check is a parity check matrix of the code, - y is a received word, - t the number of errors to correct, - e is the extension degree, - s is the dimension of the point for the vanishing ideal. Return: the system of Fitzgerald-Lax for the given decoding problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs an ideal using a generalization of Cooper’s philosophy (Fitzgerald-Lax method); see Section C.8.4. Examples illustrate building the FL system, computing std(sys) (Groebner basis reduction) and reading off solutions (error positions/values) from reduced Groebner basis 'red_sys'. Demonstrates options (redSB) and using points lists to find error positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: decodeRandomFL
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: decodeRandomFL(redun,p,e,n,t,ncodes,ntrials,minpol); - n is length of codes generated, - redun = redundancy, - p is characteristic, - e is extension degree, - t is number of errors to correct, - ncodes number of random codes to be processed, - ntrials number of received vectors per code, - minpol: minimal polynomial for the extension (may be required). Return: nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs randomized experiments using the Fitzgerald-Lax (FL) system for decoding; examples show many codeword/received word pairs and corresponding Groebner bases of the FL system. Useful for large-scale testing of FL-based decoding over random codes; notes that minimal polynomial parameter may be needed due to SINGULAR peculiarities.
